intro: Karate and taekwondo are often mixed up. They come from two different places. Karate grew on Okinawa, in the old Ryukyu Kingdom, with deep ties to China. Taekwondo was built in South Korea in the years after 1945.

In this unit, you will follow each art from small private lessons to big national groups. You will meet teachers such as Itosu Ankō, Funakoshi Gichin and Choi Hong-hi. You will see how names, ranks, headquarters and the Olympics shaped both arts.

By the end, you can explain where karate and taekwondo began and how they differ. You can name the groups that give their ranks and write their rules. You can tell a legend from a fact that records can show.
bigQuestion: How did karate and taekwondo grow from local arts into national and Olympic sports?

timeline.t: Shō Hashi unites Okinawa as the Ryukyu Kingdom
Japan makes Ryukyu into Okinawa Prefecture
Itosu Ankō helps bring the art into Okinawa's schools
Okinawan teachers in Naha agree on the empty-hand name
Korea is freed from Japanese rule; more kwans open in Seoul
The Kukkiwon opens in Seoul; Okinawa returns to Japan
The World Taekwondo Federation is founded in Seoul
Taekwondo gives its first Olympic medals in Sydney
Karate appears at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, held a year late

an older Okinawan name for the art; it means Tang hand, or China hand
what karate came to mean after the 1930s, when its written form changed
short rules or lessons for how to act, like Itosu's letter of 1908
a numbered black-belt rank, used in judo, karate and taekwondo
a Japanese word for a school or style of an art
a Korean word for a training hall or school
the way of the foot and fist; a Korean art named in 1955

choices: Okinawa, in the old Ryukyu Kingdom
test.why: Karate grew on Okinawa, the center of the Ryukyu Kingdom.

test.q: What did the old name tōde mean?
choices: the way of the foot and fist
test.why: Tōde means Tang hand, and Tang was an old name for China.

test.q: What happened to the Ryukyu Kingdom in 1879?
test.why: In 1879, Japan ended the kingdom and created Okinawa Prefecture.

test.q: Who wrote a letter of ten precepts about the art in 1908?
test.why: Itosu Ankō wrote his precepts to Okinawa's school leaders in 1908.

test.q: Why is 1922 an important year for karate?
choices: Funakoshi demonstrated the art in Tokyo
test.why: In 1922, Funakoshi Gichin showed the art in Tokyo and stayed to teach.

test.q: What does the Japanese word ryū mean?
test.why: Ryū means a school or style, as in Gōjū-ryū or Wadō-ryū.

test.q: Which marks did karate borrow from judo?
choices: the white jacket and dan ranks
test.why: In Tokyo, Funakoshi borrowed judo's white jacket and dan ranks.

choices: a Korean training hall or school
test.why: Kwan is the Korean word for a hall; the first kwans opened in Seoul in the 1940s.

test.q: Who put forward the name taekwondo in 1955?
test.why: Army general Choi Hong-hi put forward the name taekwondo in 1955.

test.q: How are karate and taekwondo different?
choices: Karate grew on Okinawa; taekwondo was built in South Korea after 1945
They are the same art with two names
Taekwondo is older than karate by 1,000 years
test.why: The two arts came from different places, with different names, ranks and headquarters.

test.q: What does the Kukkiwon give students?
test.why: The Kukkiwon in Seoul gives black-belt certificates that match across countries.

test.q: Which federation's rules are used for Olympic taekwondo?
test.why: World Taekwondo, founded in 1973, writes the Olympic rules.

test.q: What was taekwondo at the 1988 Seoul Olympics?
test.why: Taekwondo was a demonstration sport in 1988 and 1992 and gave full medals from 2000.

test.q: Which statement is a legend, not a documented fact?
test.why: Historians say modern taekwondo was built in the twentieth century.

test.q: What was special about karate at the Tokyo Games held in 2021?
choices: It was the first and so far only Olympics with karate medals
test.why: Karate was added for Tokyo 2020 and was not kept for Paris 2024.

write.prompt: Some people call taekwondo "Korean karate." Is that a fair name? Argue your answer using at least two dates or records from this unit, such as the 1936 Naha meeting, the 1955 naming of taekwondo, the 1972 opening of the Kukkiwon or the 2000 Olympics.
tips: Name each date, group or record you use.
Say where each art began: Okinawa or South Korea.
Show what the two arts share and how they differ.
Label legends as legends and set them beside the records.
Use unit words such as kwan, dan, federation and Kukkiwon.
